item.title: Reverse a Function to C
item.description: Target: Windows x86-64, MSVC-style calling convention (rcx = arg1, edx = arg2). Reverse this function to equivalent C. rcx points to an int array; edx holds its element count. find_min: mov eax, [rcx] ; eax = arr[0] | mov r8d, 1 ; i = 1 | .loop: cmp r8d, edx | jge .done | mov r9d, [rcx + r8*4] ; r9d = arr[i] | cmp r9d, eax | jge .skip | mov eax, r9d ; min = arr[i] | .skip: inc r8d | jmp .loop | .done: ret --- Answer: int find_min(int *arr, int count) { int min = arr[0]; for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) { if (arr[i] < min) { min = arr[i]; } } return min; } Explanation: eax is seeded with arr[0] and doubles as the loop's running minimum and the return value, avoiding a separate stack slot. The [rcx + r8*4] addressing mode is a scaled-index load -- r8 (the counter i) is multiplied by 4 (sizeof int) and added to the base pointer rcx, giving arr[i] without a separate multiply. The jge .skip after each comparison is the inverted form of if (arr[i] < min): the branch is taken (skipping the update) whenever the condition is false, the standard branch-on-false pattern for compiling a single if body.
